Although filtered through Mara’s viewpoint, the story presents distinct, believable perspectives: Carl confuses thoughtful attention with permission to use private material; Martin disguises romantic self-interest as concern; Lizzy values trust without offering easy forgiveness; and Johan offers attention without constant interpretation. Their flaws emerge through consistent dialogue and behavior rather than caricature. Mara’s recognition that she has repeated Carl’s kind of betrayal further complicates the moral picture without excusing either of them.
